why: The student turns the switch into an equivalent else-if chain, deduced from the code: case 1 becomes the first test, the case 2 to case 3 fall-through becomes one || condition, and default becomes the final else; the branch logic is correct, but 'elif' is Python, not Java, so the code would not compile.

concepts.quote: if (value == 1) result = 30; elif (value == 2 || value == 3) result = -10; else result = 5;
concepts.why: The else-if chain with a final catch-all else is the right structure, but Java has no 'elif' keyword; it must be 'else if'.
Covered only as part of the else-if chain.
Two comparisons are correctly joined with || into one condition, matching the grouped case labels.
Assignments are copied from the switch, not reasoned about.
Each case is correctly mapped to an equality test on the same expression, including the case 2/3 fall-through and the default.
